source.citation: Unidentified author, article on hysterical aphonia, Medical Record 52 (1897): 87. Author and title to confirm from the page image.

reported.label: Miss A. A.
reported.occupation: attendant in a hospital for the insane

complaints: woke one morning able only to whisper
presentation.course: No strain, illness, or upset beforehand; slept well. Two similar attacks years before, both of which ended by themselves. She kept working throughout.

findings: nervous temperament, very competent, good general health

treatments.response: voice returned suddenly and for good after five weeks

outcome: Full spontaneous recovery after five weeks.
quotes: on rising one morning after sleeping well and feeling in her usual health, she found she could only whisper
the attack lasted five weeks without mitigation, when it suddenly and permanently disappeared

modernReading.text: Functional (psychogenic) dysphonia. The voice is lost without damage to the larynx and often returns suddenly. A doctor should still rule out a laryngeal or nerve cause.

fixed: earlier attacks that ended by themselves

constrained.rule: a job she keeps doing in a whisper: attendant, nurse, clerk, shop assistant, servant

notes: A case where heavy treatment is not needed and may do harm. The same article has a young man mute for nine years after his father spoke sharply to him, and a woman with whispered voice and wider hysterical signs after an accident.
